content.text: I have enough to classify. Here is my assessment.

input.quote: (a) Liability for Specific Obligations. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable under this Agreement only for its specific obligations under this Agreement. All other liability is expressly waived and released as a condition of, and consideration for, the execution of this Agreement by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable only for its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement.
input.rationale:
The liability architecture here is mutual and, on its material terms, sits at or above the fallback, so no redline is warranted.

1. Mutuality: Section 6.2(a) (p0283) limits the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's liability to their specific obligations and to their own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence. Section 5.2(a) (p0243) applies word-for-word the same limitation to the Depositor. The limitation is therefore symmetrical and not a one-sided vendor shield — the walk-away scenario (our liability uncapped while the counterparty's is capped) does not arise.

2. No monetary cap on the counterparty: there is no dollar or months-of-fees cap anywhere in the Agreement (no "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed" or consequential-damages exclusion language; the only damages limitation found is the arbitral panel's limited remedial power at p0469). For us this is better than the preferred 12-months'-fees / USD 1,000,000 formulation. Importing a fees-based cap would be actively adverse: the Servicing Fee in this structure is a small monthly percentage of principal balance, so a 12-month-fees cap would be illusory and would materially reduce Cellco's exposure. Consistent with the rule's own warning about caps measured against a small fee base, we should not propose one.

3. Carve-outs: the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's indemnities under Section 6.3(a) (p0291, p0292) run to the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, damages and liabilities resulting from willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, with no cap and no super-cap ceiling. Indemnification, gross negligence and willful misconduct — the fallback's minimum carve-out set — are all outside any limitation, and "bad faith" substantially covers the fraud carve-out.

4. Our side is additionally protected: Section 9.6 (p0378) limits any claim against the Depositor or the Issuer to the Depositor Transferred Property, an effective ceiling on our exposure that the counterparty does not enjoy.

Noted but not flagged (minor sub-elements per the classification rules): there is no express uncapped carve-out for confidentiality, data protection/security or infringement of our IP, no separate fraud carve-out beyond "bad faith", and no mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion. Given that the counterparty carries no monetary cap at all and its indemnities are uncapped, these omissions do not defeat the fallback and are recorded for information rather than redlined. This is a securitization transfer and servicing agreement rather than a commercial supply contract, and the exculpation-plus-uncapped-indemnity model is the market-standard equivalent of the playbook position.
